text:
Maya (Product): Quick q — traveling to Tokyo + Seoul next month. My company card charges a 3% foreign transaction fee. Policy on claiming those FX fees? Also thinking about requesting a cash advance for local per-diem and taxis.

Ava (People Ops): FX fees on company card are not reimbursable (card benefit). If you're using a personal card and getting charged FX fees, you can claim them but must attach the card statement showing the fee line item.

Maya (Product): I plan to use personal for a cheaper fare. Will submit the card statement, but the statement groups fees under "Misc charges" without line-level detail. Will that pass?

Diego - Finance: We need a clear fee line or a bank's fee breakdown PDF. If the issuer groups it, ask the bank for a transaction breakdown or screenshot from online banking showing the fee. Without that, we may reject the fee reimbursement.

Nina (Manager): If getting the bank doc will delay, consider requesting a small travel advance to avoid out-of-pocket FX.

Maya (Product): How do advances work for multi-country trips? I need per-diem + metro cards in both cities.

Ava (People Ops): Request an advance via the Travel Advance form: https://redwood.company/travel-advance. Choose "multi-country per-diem" and list estimated local currency amounts per city. We convert to USD at the bank rate on date of advance.

Diego - Finance: Note advance amounts are netted against final expenses. If you overspend, reimbursements cover the difference. If underspent, you must return leftover funds or we'll deduct from next payroll after 30 days.

Maya (Product): Good to know. What about receipts: some small vendors in Seoul don't provide itemized receipts (just a stamp). The hotel folio only shows a lump lodging charge without nightly breakdown.

Ava (People Ops): For small vendor items under KRW/USD equivalent of $20, an attestation + photo is allowed. For lodging, we need the hotel folio showing dates and total; if nightly rates not split, submit the folio + booking confirmation showing per-night rate (booking engine email) or ask hotel for an itemized folio.

Diego - Finance: If the vendor truly cannot itemize, include the vendor contact and reason in the claim. Finance may accept on a case-by-case basis but keep evidence (photos, emails).

Maya (Product): One more: I had a client dinner in Tokyo — some meals are client entertainment vs regular meals. Which category to choose?

Nina (Manager): Mark as "Client Entertainment" and include attendees + business purpose. Pre-approval recommended for dinners > $150 per person.

Ava (People Ops): Tip policy: reasonable local tipping is reimbursable; add it to the meal receipt when possible. For cash tips without receipt, include an attestation and secondary evidence (credit card total showing amount + explanation).

ExpenseBot: Friendly reminder: submit Travel Preapproval before you depart to speed reimbursement. Preapproval link: https://redwood.company/travel-preapproval. Must attach: itinerary, estimated per-diem by city, currency estimates, and any expected visa or FX fees. Missing preapproval can delay payout. :alarm_clock:

Maya (Product): Thanks — I'll file preapproval and request a $900 advance (split: JPY 40k, KRW 80k). CC'ing Nina.

Diego - Finance: I'll review once preapproval is in. For FX claims, include both the foreign amount and USD conversion line from your card or bank. We use daily bank rate at transaction date.

Ava (People Ops): If bank documentation isn't available for the FX fee, escalate to People Ops and Finance together before filing.

Maya (Product): Will do. Appreciate it! :pray:
